explanation.en:
同じ (おなじ) means “same.” It is used to say that two things are the same. It behaves like a な-adjective, but it does not take な before a noun.

Key points:
• Pattern: A は B と 同じ です
• と connects the two things being compared
• 同じ acts like a noun/na-adjective but no な before noun
• Very common for identity or similarity

Example: “この本はあの本と同じです” means “This book is the same as that book.”

You can also use it with people: “私とあなたは同じ学校です” (We are from the same school).

Remember: do not add な before nouns (❌ 同じな本). Just use 同じ + noun: “同じ本.”

Practice by comparing things around you: 同じ色, 同じ名前, 同じクラス.

structure.pattern: A は B と 同じ (Noun) です

examples.japanese: この本はあの本と同じです。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa ano hon to onaji desu.
examples.english: This book is the same as that book.

examples.japanese: 私とあなたは同じ学校です。
examples.romaji: Watashi to anata wa onaji gakkou desu.
examples.english: You and I are at the same school.

examples.japanese: このペンはそのペンと同じ色です。
examples.romaji: Kono pen wa sono pen to onaji iro desu.
examples.english: This pen is the same color as that pen.

examples.japanese: 田中さんは私と同じクラスです。
examples.romaji: Tanaka-san wa watashi to onaji kurasu desu.
examples.english: Tanaka-san is in the same class as me.

commonMistakes.correction: Do not add な after 同じ

commonMistakes.mistake: Using が instead of と for comparison
commonMistakes.correction: Use と to connect the two items
commonMistakes.example: ❌ この本はあの本が同じ → ✅ この本はあの本と同じ
